author: Pedini
text:
Hi mate. You have some really good questions. For your first question,
 from the chart available, we actually don't know whether box A or box 1
 is more important (second chart) because we can't see any history on
the left. We need to know if price is breaking important levels before
we can say price made a valid FTR. (You can read the SD article on
markepedia to get an idea of what i mean). For us to say that D is a
valid FTR we need to be sure that box 1 is an important level. If box
one is an important level then the break of it creates a nice FTR.

Hope this is of some help,

Peds.

author: charlespips
text:
Hi TinkerBelle,

I think IF's chart explained about "what's origin":

My thought is, If FTR formed after breaking key levels (not just recent
low/high), this FTR become Important. Price would respect it first,
before breaking it and aiming for the next important FTR above/below, or
 the origin.

As per Kovalenko's chart, you can see box1 is important because it break
 key SR level. Therefore, the last DP, which is the FL (red box 2) in an
 important one. When broken, the new FL/FTR (FTR 3) become significant
as well.

As for why not XYZ, instead of FTR3 in your chart, the FL/FTR3 is a
strong D zone that broke red box FL. the XYZ and B boxes you drew are CP
 zone if I'm not mistaken, as there is no clean D zone.

FTR 3 is (for me) exactly the edge of CPPAZ. If engulfed, it will slide
through even further down past your XYZ zone (I haven't check the left),
 right to the source of the move/FTR down below. But no, price can't
break the level because it's strong, and up she goes. I think it's also a
 FO because there is an engulf of the opposite FTR in box 1.

Please kindly correct me if I'm wrong.

Happy weekend, everyone!

author: By_Tor2114
text:
How do we define whether or not something is an important level, so as
 to decide whether or not something makes a valid FTR? A level that
appears important on an M15 chart might have no relevance on a H1 chart.
 The same could be say for a level that looks important on H4, but looks
 like nothing on Weekly.

EDIT: Also, how can we be sure when an FTR has formed? A level might
break, and an FTR could form on an M5 chart which turns out to be of no
use. However, a larger FTR could then be formed on M30 that later turns
price very nicely.

text:
The other thing I was going to say about putting more weight on a HTF
FTR is how do we know when it has formed? We might see one appear on M5,
 then decide to wait for one to appear on M15. Should we then wait to
see if one appears on M30, H1, H4, etc, etc? By the time we have waited
for a HTF FTR to appear, it might be the the lower TF was the correct
one. There would be no way to know this in real time.
